lines.text: Parallel parking looks hard, but it's just three steering moves.
Find a space about one and a half car lengths long.
Signal right and stop beside the front car, about 2–3 feet away.
Line up your rear bumper with its rear bumper.
Check behind you, then reverse slowly with the wheel turned fully right.
Stop when your car is at about 45° to the curb.
Straighten the wheel and back up in a straight line.
Stop when your front bumper clears the car ahead.
Now turn the wheel fully left and keep reversing.
The front swings in and your car lines up with the curb.
Straighten the wheels and pull forward to center in the space.
Aim for about a foot from the curb.
Go slow, keep checking your mirrors, and remember: right, straight, left.
